title: The shared-space work session — question explanation
learningObjective: Protect remote sessions, devices and information in mixed work environments
format: 16:9 educational motion-graphics video; narration; separate captions; no autoplay with sound
visualStyle: Deep navy and charcoal; restrained cyan/electric-blue highlights; limited purple accents; clean typography; purposeful, low-motion transitions; accessible contrast.

scenes.name: Scenario setup
scenes.visual: You are working in a shared café. Your laptop is unlocked while you step away, a sensitive dashboard is visible, and you are connected to public Wi-Fi.
scenes.direction: Show a fictional simulated setting. Use generic UI and no actual organization, brand, user identity, credential, real URL or live account.

scenes.name: Learning objective and risk cue
scenes.visual: Protect remote sessions, devices and information in mixed work environments
scenes.direction: Highlight only observable cues and explain the decision context without implying certainty beyond the scenario.

scenes.name: Recommended response
scenes.visual: Option B: Lock the device before stepping away, keep it physically controlled, use a trusted connection and follow remote-access policy. Physical access, screen exposure and network risks require layered controls.
scenes.direction: Animate the recommended defensive choice as a clear decision path. Display the action verb and trusted channel/control.

scenes.name: Why the other options fail
scenes.visual: Option A: Minimizing a window does not protect the unattended device or session. Option C: Removing automatic locking increases the opportunity for unauthorized access. Option D: An unknown bystander is not an appropriate security control.
scenes.direction: Show each unsafe alternative separately with a complete, concise reason. Do not depict operational exploitation, malicious code or credential capture.

scenes.name: Defensive takeaway
scenes.visual: Lock the screen whenever unattended, keep devices in your control, avoid exposing sensitive content and use the approved secure connection method. Remote work combines physical, visual and network risks; use layered protection.
scenes.direction: Close with one readable takeaway and the next safe action. Keep the final frame long enough for comprehension.

narration: Scenario: You are working in a shared café. Your laptop is unlocked while you step away, a sensitive dashboard is visible, and you are connected to public Wi-Fi. Safest response: Option B: Lock the device before stepping away, keep it physically controlled, use a trusted connection and follow remote-access policy. Physical access, screen exposure and network risks require layered controls. Option A is unsafe because Minimizing a window does not protect the unattended device or session. Option C is unsafe because Removing automatic locking increases the opportunity for unauthorized access. Option D is unsafe because An unknown bystander is not an appropriate security control. In practice: Lock the screen whenever unattended, keep devices in your control, avoid exposing sensitive content and use the approved secure connection method. Key takeaway: Remote work combines physical, visual and network risks; use layered protection.
